key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings with better droplet spreading form denser microstructures that improve corrosion resistance and reduce wear, especially in humid environments.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray parameters and controlling porosity can extend the service life of Fe-based protective coatings on carbon steel in corrosive and tribological applications.
method: Prepared Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spray under different spraying parameters.
Evaluated coating microstructure, long-term corrosion behavior, and tribological performance across humidity conditions.
Related droplet morphology, porosity, and tribo-chemical interactions to corrosion and wear outcomes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic corrosion and wear testing showing that higher porosity worsens long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity lowers friction coefficient and wear rate.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on spray parameter control and humidity; scaling to service conditions may require careful validation of porosity and environmental variability.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
